name: Kunming Changshui International Airport
before:
The gateway to south west China and on to Southeast and South Asia, 24.5 km north east of Kunming. It handled 49.7 million passengers in 2025, tenth busiest in China.

The altitude is worth knowing. The airport sits in graded mountainous ground about 2,100 metres above sea level, which affects aircraft performance and can make arrivals feel different to a sea level airport.

The scale inside is considerable. The main terminal covers 548,300 square metres and is the second largest terminal building in China, with 66 jet bridge gates out of 88 gates in total. Trams nicknamed Green Dolphin move passengers along a 1.88 km line inside.

It is a hub for China Eastern, Kunming Airlines, Lucky Air, Sichuan Airlines and Ruili Airlines, with two runways of 4.5 km and 4 km.

Punctuality is better than most: the airport was the first in China to adopt collaborative decision making with airlines, and on-time performance reached 85.3 per cent in 2017.

It opened on 28 June 2012, replacing the old Wujiaba airport, which was demolished.
after:
A hub for south west China and for flights on to Southeast and South Asia, 24.5 km north east of Kunming. It handled 49.7 million passengers in 2025, tenth busiest in China.

The altitude is worth knowing: the airport sits about 2,100 metres above sea level.

China Eastern, Kunming Airlines, Lucky Air, Sichuan Airlines and Ruili Airlines all have bases here, and there are two runways of 4.5 km and 4 km.

It opened on 28 June 2012, replacing the old Wujiaba airport.

claims.claim: a hub for south west China and for flights on to Southeast and South Asia
claims.inAfter: A hub for south west China and for flights on to Southeast and South Asia
claims.note: Was 'The gateway to south west China and on to Southeast and South Asia'; 'gateway to' is a banned phrase. The operator calls it one of China's eight regional hub airports and its international hub for South and Southeast Asia; Yunnan.cn (December 2025) describes a network covering South, Southeast and East Asia and reaching the Middle East.

The operator lists six base airlines: China Eastern's Yunnan company, Lucky Air, Kunming Airlines, Sichuan Airlines' Yunnan branch, China Southern's Yunnan branch and Sunan Ruili Airlines (苏南瑞丽航空, which Kunming's bus operator calls Ruili Airlines); China Southern, which the old text left out, is not added. Kunming's bus operator named stops at the Kunming Airlines and Lucky Air, Ruili Airlines, Sichuan Airlines and China Eastern premises on the airport site in November 2025.

claims.claim: The gateway to south west China
claims.wasBefore: The gateway to south west China and on to Southeast and South Asia
claims.why: 'Gateway to' is a banned phrase; reworded as a hub (see above).

claims.claim: graded mountainous ground; the altitude affects aircraft performance and arrivals
claims.wasBefore: The airport sits in graded mountainous ground about 2,100 metres above sea level, which affects aircraft performance and can make arrivals feel different to a sea level airport.
claims.why: The elevation is kept (OurAirports, Wikipedia). 'Graded mountainous ground' rests on Wikipedia alone, and no source read here says how the altitude affects aircraft or arrivals.

claims.claim: terminal 548,300 square metres, second largest in China
claims.wasBefore: The main terminal covers 548,300 square metres and is the second largest terminal building in China
claims.why: Sources disagree: Wikipedia gives 548,300 m2, Airport Technology (2012) 423,500 m2 and 'the biggest terminal in Greater China' at the time. The ranking is stale either way: Guangzhou's Terminal 2 (over 808,700 m2, opened 2018, Wikipedia) and Hangzhou's Terminal 4 (720,000 m2, opened 2022, its operator), both saved in this sweep, are larger than either figure.

claims.wasBefore: with 66 jet bridge gates out of 88 gates in total
claims.why: Sources disagree: Wikipedia gives 66 gates with jet bridges, Airport Technology says ThyssenKrupp supplied 77 boarding bridges.
The old text's lead-in to the terminal figures, which are cut.

claims.claim: Green Dolphin trams on a 1.88 km line
claims.wasBefore: Trams nicknamed Green Dolphin move passengers along a 1.88 km line inside.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone; the operator's pages read here do not mention the people mover.

claims.wasBefore: It is a hub for China Eastern, Kunming Airlines, Lucky Air, Sichuan Airlines and Ruili Airlines
claims.why: Reworded to 'all have bases here', the operator's own term (see above).

claims.claim: punctuality: first in China with collaborative decision making; 85.3 per cent on time in 2017
claims.wasBefore: Punctuality is better than most: the airport was the first in China to adopt collaborative decision making with airlines, and on-time performance reached 85.3 per cent in 2017.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone, and the punctuality figure is nine years old, so 'better than most' has nothing current behind it.
Wikipedia says it was later demolished; Airport Technology (2012) says only that it was set to be dismantled. No second source for the demolition itself.

opinion.why: The old text's advice, kept on the confirmed elevation of about 2,100 m (OurAirports 2,104 m).
